provenance.note: Semantics are copied verbatim from the reference implementation so the first migration cannot change behaviour. No code was added, renamed, or re-classified.
provenance.http_status_from: growth-tactics/api/failure.py, wisent-backend-images/app/failure.py and wisent-customer-support/src/failure.js, which held three identical copies of this mapping. Verbatim: every entry agreed before it moved here.
provenance.exit_code_from: wisent-compute/stado-rs/src/failure.rs, probierz/agent/failure.mjs and wisent-tools/wisent/failure.py, which held the same rule three times.

codes.operator_summary: our deployment configuration is incomplete or wrong
codes.meaning: A value the process needs was absent or malformed. Ours to fix, and no amount of retrying changes it.

codes.operator_summary: the credentials this command used were rejected
codes.meaning: An upstream refused the identity we presented. Retrying with the same credential repeats the refusal.

codes.operator_summary: what the command asked for is not there
codes.meaning: The request named something absent. A server error is never classified here: collapsing 5xx into 'nothing there' is what let a storage outage read as an empty queue.
The request was well formed and refused for pace. Worth repeating later, unchanged.

codes.operator_summary: an upstream did not answer in time
codes.meaning: No verdict arrived. The operation may or may not have happened, which is why it counts as our outage.

codes.operator_summary: infrastructure we depend on is unreachable
codes.meaning: A dependency did not answer at all. Nothing about the request was wrong.

codes.operator_summary: the command failed and we could not attribute the failure
codes.meaning: The last resort. A failure that stays unknown is a gap in classification, not a kind of failure, and it is worth reading as a defect in whoever emitted it.

upstream_status.note: Classification of a status an upstream answered one of our calls with. Ranges are inclusive.

exit_code.note: What a command exits with. Only the retryable path is remapped: a caller that already chose an exit code keeps it, so a CLI's own conventions survive adoption.
exit_code.rule: retryable codes exit with `retry`; every other code keeps the exit code the caller already chose

failure_point.grammar: a dotted lowercase path, one segment or more
failure_point.note: The depth carries no meaning and this rule stopped pretending it does. It was <service>.<surface>.<operation>, exactly three segments, which was invented from examples rather than read out of the registries -- and it moved twice in one hour when the migrations reached them: probierz and growth-tactics are two-segment, stado's ids come from the clap subcommand path and run from one segment (`cli`) to four (`cli.host.user.create`). A grammar that refuses what five products already emit is the package being wrong. What is validated is the shape, because that is all a shared rule can honestly check: lowercase, dot-separated, no empty segment. The product is not required as a segment because `service` is already a field of every envelope.
